_note: Current 2026 general-election candidates for U.S. Senate, U.S. House and the statewide offices the roster already tracks, in every state outside Utah, read from each state's official candidate list or certified ballot on 2026-10-21. Read by scripts/test-roster-candidates-2026-oct.mjs and scripts/test-depth-no-score-drift.mjs.

al.reason: Skipped. The Alabama Secretary of State's 8/26/2026 certifications of Democratic, special-primary and independent candidates are scanned images with no readable text layer in this environment; the names could not be verified against the documents, so none are used. Alabama Secretary of State's 8/26/2026 state certifications of Republican, Democratic and Independent candidates for the Nov 3, 2026 general election (scanned PDFs, transcribed by hand). CD 1, 2, 6 and 7 nominees come from the Aug 11, 2026 special primary (party lists in the same certifications); the Democratic names follow the 8/24/2026 amended list (e.g. 'Clyde Jones', 'Terri Sewell'); no independent or minor-party candidates were certified for these offices. Later amendments (8/28 and 9/2 ALGOP) touch only HD 51 and SD 25.

ak.note: Alaska Division of Elections official candidate list for the 2026 General Election (page last updated Sept 25, 2026; withdrawal deadline Aug 31, 2026); all listed candidates marked (Certified). Certified write-in candidates excluded. Governor runs on a joint ticket; name is the gubernatorial candidate only, party string is as printed for the ticket. Alaska's Attorney General is appointed, not elected, so no AG race.

az.reason: All Arizona SOS domains (azsos.gov, apps.azsos.gov, results.arizona.vote, arizona.vote) return a Cloudflare 403 challenge to both curl and the fetch tool, including the 2026 Election Info page, the primary canvass and the general write-in/withdrawn list (azsos.gov/media/718). The Wayback Machine holds only the pre-primary 2026-Candidate-Nominations-and-Petitions-Filed-0330.pdf, which does not identify primary winners. No general-election nominee list could be retrieved from an official source.

ar.note: Arkansas Secretary of State's official election-night results system (arkansas.tally-enr.com, linked from sos.arkansas.gov Election Results), pre-loaded with the '2026 General Election & Judical Runoff' (Nov 3, 2026) ballot contests; data last updated 2026-10-20, not a signed certification. Names printed with a party-code prefix (e.g. 'REP Tom Cotton') which was stripped; party taken from the election's party table. AG Tim Griffin is unopposed but appears on the ballot.

ca.note: California Secretary of State 'Official Certified List of Candidates' for the November 3, 2026 General Election (PDF), certified by Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber on August 27, 2026. Top-two system, so some contests have two candidates of the same party; no U.S. Senate contest is on the 2026 California ballot. Asterisks (incumbent markers) were stripped from names.

co.note: Colorado Secretary of State "2026 General Election Official Candidate List" (HTML table; XLSX version also published), official as certified to the counties on September 4, 2026. Certified write-in candidates (Write in? = Y) and struck-through (withdrawn) entries excluded; no federal/statewide entry was struck through. Lt. Governor running mates not included (not in scope).

ct.note: CT Secretary of the State has not posted a consolidated 2026 List of Candidates (its 'Filed Candidates' page still shows 2014). Compiled from the SOTS-published official town sample ballots for the Nov 3, 2026 State Election (134 town PDFs parsed, covering all 5 congressional districts; names/party lines as printed on the ballots), cross-checked against Appendix II '2026 Candidates' of the SOTS 2026 Voter Guide, which agrees on every candidate and party line. Fusion voting: 'party' lists every ballot line held, comma-separated. No U.S. Senate race in CT in 2026; Lt. Governor running mates (Susan Bysiewicz, Matt Corey) omitted per scope.json.

de.note: Delaware Department of Elections 'General Election 11/3/2026 - Filed Candidates by Office' HTML table (Last Updated: 2026-10-21 08:56 AM); included status 'Qualified' only, excluded Lee Murphy (Withdrawn). Governor is not on the 2026 ballot (next election 2028); the linked xlsx export was blocked (Request Rejected), so the HTML table was used.

fl.note: Florida Division of Elections Candidate Tracking System tab-delimited export for election 20261103-GEN (state candidates, all offices/statuses), filtered to Qualified/Unopposed and excluding Write-In; the qualifying period has closed and primaries are done, but the DOS does not publish a separate certified-ballot list. U.S. Senate marked special=true because it fills Rubio's unexpired term (appointee Ashley Moody), though the DOS lists it only as 'United States Senator'; CD-10 Maxwell Frost is 'Unopposed' (deemed elected, not printed on ballot); Lt. ga.note: sos.ga.gov (qualified-candidate search, general-election ballot list, My Voter Page) blocks automated access via Cloudflare, so this list is built from official county election-office consolidated/composite sample ballots for the Nov 3, 2026 general (posted Sept-Oct 2026), one county per congressional district. Every county ballot shows only Republican and Democratic nominees for these offices, and the SOS certified write-ins (9/15/2026) are excluded. Party labels and name casing are as printed on each county ballot (White County prints all caps with 'Rep'/'Dem'); office_as_listed for counties other than Fulton and White is normalized to the common GA ballot wording.

hi.note: Hawaii Office of Elections 2026 Candidate Report (CSV export from olvr.hawaii.gov, report last updated Sept 4, 2026); only entries with status 'In General' kept (primary losers 'In Primary', withdrawn and void excluded). No U.S. Senate seat is up in Hawaii in 2026, and the Attorney General is appointed, not elected.

id.note: Idaho Secretary of State candidate filing portal (run.voteidaho.gov) public "Search Candidates" data for election "11/03/2026 - 2026 GENERAL" (backend POST https://api-run.voteidaho.gov/api/FiledCandidates/SearchCandidates), which reports isFinalList=true (SOS certification deadline was Sept 4, 2026). Kept filingStatus=Approved and non-write-in; excluded withdrawn (David Roth, US Senate D; C. Sierra, US House 2) and write-in Jacob Burnett (Governor). "Pro-Life" (Constitution, Governor) is the candidate's legal name as listed.

il.note: Illinois State Board of Elections candidate data file (tab-delimited GE20261103.txt) for the 11/3/2026 General Election, downloaded 2026-10-21. The SBE certified the ballot on Aug 21, 2026. Only 'Active' records are kept; Removed and Withdrawn are dropped. Names are built as FirstName + LastName from the file's fields. Governor comes from the joint 'GOVERNOR AND LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR' ticket: the running-mate rows, which name the governor in AffiliateCommittee, are omitted because Lt. Governor is out of scope. The file has no write-in records.

The list has no status column; write-in candidates (party 'Write-In (...)') were excluded: Andrew Delano, Alexander R (Alex) Degman, Prescription Dope Deaths Johnson, Jr, David E. ia.note: Iowa SOS 'Candidate List, November 3, 2026 General Election' PDF (last updated 8/19/2026, the post-primary vacancy-filling deadline). sos.iowa.gov blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403), so the identical official PDF was retrieved from the Internet Archive capture of 2026-09-23; a later revision on sos.iowa.gov, if any, could not be checked.

ks.reason: The only official general-election candidate list is the Kansas SOS 'Candidate List' (https://sos.ks.gov/elections/elections_upcoming_candidate.aspx), which is behind an AWS WAF JavaScript challenge (HTTP 202/403 to curl and WebFetch), and no headless browser is available. The SOS site, press releases and the 26elec folder have no static/PDF general candidate list. The official 2026 Primary Official Vote Totals PDF (sos.ks.gov/elections/26elec/2026-Primary-Election-Official-Vote-Totals.pdf) covers only the D/R primaries, not Libertarian/United Kansas convention nominees or independents (filed by Aug 3), so it was not used.

ky.note: Kentucky Secretary of State Candidate Filings database, '2026 General Election' (office pages for US Senator and US Representative); Write-In filers and the Withdrawn/Deceased/Disqualified section (Mohammad Wael Ahmad, KY-4) excluded. No Governor, Attorney General or Secretary of State contests in KY in 2026 (next in 2027). This is the filings database, not a separately certified ballot list.

la.note: Louisiana SOS official election-results data feed (voterportal.sos.la.gov) for the Nov 3, 2026 election, pre-loaded with races and qualified candidates (file WriteTime 2026-10-21). Party codes (DEM/REP/NOPTY/LBT) expanded. Governor and Attorney General are not on the 2026 ballot (next elected 2027).

oh.reason: Every ohiosos.gov URL tried returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare managed challenge / 'Website Maintenance' page), for both curl and the fetch tool. or.note: ORESTAR (Oregon SOS Elections Division) Candidate Filings export for the 2026 General Election, qualified filings only (disqualified excluded); minor-party/nominating deadline was Aug 25, 2026. Oregon's Attorney General is not on the 2026 ballot (elected 2024).

pa.reason: The official 2026 general candidate list is only in the PA DOS candidate database at pavoterservices.pa.gov ('Official Candidate Listing - Post Primary/Post Ballot Lottery' reports and the Basic/Advanced Search). Incapsula bot protection blocks it for curl, and fetched pages showed only office headings or a bot-check page. pa.gov posts no static 2026 general candidate list, only the post-primary withdrawal listing (9/7/2026), the objection tracker and the calendar. No U.S. Senate, Attorney General or Secretary of State race applies (SoS is appointed; AG was elected in 2024).

ri.note: No consolidated certified general-election list could be retrieved: vote.sos.ri.gov and elections.ri.gov HTML pages (candidate search, sample ballots) are behind a Cloudflare bot challenge. Party labels follow the xlsx ('Democrat','Republican','Independent'). Independent names are assembled from the xlsx first/middle/last fields exactly as given (e.g. 'C D Reynolds' is how the source records him); primary-nominee names are as printed in the results, with the results' '*' marker dropped. Caveat: post-primary withdrawals or replacements would not appear in either source. RI-2 has no independent; Lt. Governor omitted per scope.json.
